codemap:
Codemap for "A session timeline as the argus UI's central view". Every file the issue has to change, path and why. Collector work is in tools/argus, interface work in tools/argus-ui, per the issue's own split.

Collector — content in
- tools/argus/src/claude.mjs — holds `otelEnvFor`, the env block `argus env` prints, and the EVENT/SPAN/attribute constants (`api_request_body`, `api_response_body`, `agent.name`, `toolParametersOf`) the content flags and the timeline are named by.
- tools/argus/bin/argus.mjs — the `env` command and its four output formats (shell, json, dotenv, settings) plus the setup and tunnel paths that print the same block; its help text describes what the block sets.
- tools/argus/src/store.mjs — the in-memory store: ingests every record, aggregates per session, holds the bounded log/span/metric windows and answers `queryEvents`/`getSession`; the content-bearing records and any per-agent, per-time view of them live here.
- tools/argus/src/server.mjs — the JSON API (`/api/sessions`, `/api/events`, `/api/metrics`, `/api/traces/:id`, `/api/stream`) the UI is the only client of; whatever the timeline asks for is served from here.
- tools/argus/src/persist.mjs — appends every normalized record as JSONL and loads a measurement back; request/response bodies multiply record size, and the rotation cap plus the single kept generation decide how much of a recorded session survives to be scrubbed.
- tools/argus/scripts/demo-emit.mjs — the synthetic session generator used to see the UI without a real agent run; it emits no agent attribution and no body events, so the timeline has nothing to draw from it as it stands.

Collector — tests
- tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs — the pure-function suite that pins what the `otelEnvFor` block does and does not carry.
- tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs — the store's ingest, aggregation and query suite.
- tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs — the API suite over a real server on port 0.
- tools/argus/test/persist.test.mjs — the append/rotate/load suite.
- tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md — the suite page that owns this project's test conventions and lists the suite file by file; it grows a line whenever the suite does.

Interface
- tools/argus-ui/public/app.js — the whole page in one file: state, session list, the tab set (overview, traces, events, metrics, raw) and every renderer; the timeline view, its lanes, the time control and the selection detail all land here or in modules split out of it.
- tools/argus-ui/public/index.html — the served page shell: topbar, sidebar and the `detail` section the views mount into.
- tools/argus-ui/public/styles.css — every class the page renders; lanes, activity, a context curve, a playhead and a collapsible message list have no styling yet.
- tools/argus-ui/test/independence.test.mjs — the project-independence suite, and today the only coverage over `public/` at all, through source-text guards.
- tools/argus-ui/test/server.test.mjs — the proxy suite, including a source-text guard that the proxy names no route under `/api/`.
- tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md — the suite page: it records that there is no suite over `public/` and what happens to that rule when pure functions are pulled out of `app.js`.

Documentation
- tools/argus/README.md — states that `argus env` deliberately does not set the content flags ("Content and privacy"), and carries the API route table and the signal/flag table.
- tools/argus-ui/README.md — describes the page's views (Overview, Traces, Events, Metrics, Raw) as the interface's structure.
- skills/argus/SKILL.md — the procedure a session follows to measure itself, with its own API route table.

increments.title: Content arrives: the env block turns it on and the API serves it
increments.goal: Make the content the timeline needs actually reach the UI: `argus env` sets the content flags by default in every format it prints, and the collector keeps the content-bearing records and serves them over the JSON API with the attribution and timing a per-agent, per-time question needs.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in every format it prints: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag(s) the CLI requires to emit `claude_code.api_request_body` / `claude_code.api_response_body`.

The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed; if request/response body events turn out not to be emittable by the current CLI, that is recorded as a finding and stated as what the context view will be built from instead.
The collector stores what those events carry and exposes the content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, so a client can ask for the context belonging to a point in time.
What agent attribution actually arrives on subagent activity and on request bodies is verified against real or emitted telemetry, and any gap is recorded as a finding rather than papered over.

Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback path, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behaviour for them — this holds for the whole run and is checked here, where content first enters.
`./test.sh` is green — the standing gate every later increment inherits by the definition of a finished increment, recorded here so it belongs to exactly one.

return.plan:
# Increment 1 — content arrives: the env block turns it on, the API serves it

## Verified facts this plan rests on (real telemetry, not assumption)

Method: a local collector (`node bin/argus.mjs --port 4319 --persist <tmp>`) plus a real
child run `claude -p "…launch one general-purpose subagent that runs 'echo hello' with
Bash…" --model haiku` with every content flag set, Claude Code 2.1.226. 28 log events, 12
spans and 28 metric points were captured to JSONL and read back. Findings:

1. **The body flag is `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES`.** `=1` emits inline bodies;
   `=file:<dir>` writes them to disk and puts a `body_ref` path in the event. Verified
   emittable: 5 `claude_code.api_request_body` and 5 `claude_code.api_response_body`
   events arrived. So the issue's fallback clause ("if bodies turn out not to be
   emittable") does not apply — bodies are the context source.
2. **`agent.name` does NOT arrive on body events.** The monitoring documentation lists
   `agent.name`/`skill.name`/`plugin.name`… as attributes of `api_request_body` and
   `api_response_body`; not one of the ten captured body events carried any of them.
   This is the attribution gap the issue asked to be recorded rather than papered over.
3. **What body events do carry** is `query_source`: `sdk` for the main session,
   `agent:builtin:general-purpose` for the subagent. Plus `model`, `body`,
   `body_length`, `body_truncated`, `prompt.id`, and (response only) `request_id`.
   So the agent *type* is recoverable from bodies alone, by parsing `query_source`.
4. **`agent.name=general-purpose` does arrive — on `claude_code.api_request`**, the
   metadata event, for subagent traffic only. Main-session `api_request` events carry no
   `agent.name`. So the two sibling events disagree about attribution.
5. **No span carries `agent.name`.** Subagent spans (`claude_code.llm_request`,
   `claude_code.tool`) carry `agent_id=<opaque hex>`; the `claude_code.tool` span of
   the dispatching `Agent` tool call carries `subagent_type=general-purpose`; every
   subagent span hangs beneath that call's `claude_code.tool.execution` span.
6. **The `spanId` on a subagent's log events is the `tool.execution` span id of its
   `Agent` call**, identical across all of that subagent's events. It is the only
   per-instance key available on log records, and it is what separates two concurrent
   subagents of the same type (which share `query_source` and `agent.name`).
7. **`claude_code.tool_decision` and `claude_code.tool_result` carry no agent
   attribution at all.** `tool_result` of the subagent's Bash call sat on the execution
   span id (attributable); `tool_decision` sat on the `tool.blocked_on_user` span, a
   grandchild — attributable only by walking the span parent chain.
8. **Truncation makes a body unusable.** With `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH=61440`
   (the CLI default) the main session's request bodies arrived with
   `body_length=113845, body_truncated=true` — cut mid-JSON, so not parseable into a
   message list. The env block therefore has to raise that limit.
9. **`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT` puts tool output on span events**, not log events: the Bash
   span carried an event `tool.output` with `{bash_command, output}`. The documentation
   states it requires tracing.
10. **Events seen that `claude.mjs` does not name**: `claude_code.subagent_completed`
    (`agent_type`, `agent.source`, `duration_ms`, `total_tokens`, `total_tool_uses`,
    `is_built_in`, `is_async`), `hook_execution_start`, `hook_execution_complete`,
    `hook_registered`. Only `subagent_completed` is worth a constant here.
11. `tool_result` carries `tool_input` (full parameters, `tool_input_size_bytes`);
    `tool_decision` carries a different, reduced `tool_parameters`
    (`{"bash_command":"echo","full_command":"echo hello"}`). `toolParametersOf` already
    prefers `tool_input`, which is the right order.

## 1. `src/claude.mjs`

**`otelEnvFor`** gains, unconditionally:
`OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS='1'`, `OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES='1'`,
`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS='1'`, `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES='1'`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH='1000000'`.
Inside the existing `if (traces)` branch it also gains `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT='1'`,
because the documentation says that flag requires tracing and it writes into span events —
with `--traces false` it would be a variable that does nothing.

Decisions behind the values:
- `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES='1'` (inline), **not** `file:<dir>`. File mode gives
  untruncated bodies but leaves them on the *agent's* disk with only a path in the event;
  the collector reaches an agent over HTTP and may be on another machine, so it could not
  read them. Rejected for that reason, and recorded here so it is not re-litigated.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH='1000000'` (~1M UTF-16 units, ≈250k tokens of
  JSON). The CLI default of 61440 demonstrably truncated a 113845-character body mid-JSON
  (finding 8), which no message-list renderer can parse. Rejected: leaving the default
  (unparseable contexts), and 2000000 (a single event then approaches 4 MB and several in
  one export batch approach the collector's 32 MB body cap).
- `OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES='1'` is set explicitly even though it falls back to
  `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS` when unset, so the block states what it turns on.
- **No opt-out flag** (`--no-content`/`--content`). The issue decided content is the
  default; an opt-out would add a config layer nobody asked for and would create exactly
  the flagless recordings criterion 5 puts out of contract.

**Constants and helpers** added to the same module:
- `EVENT.subagentCompleted = 'claude_code.subagent_completed'`.
- `export const CONTENT_EVENTS = new Set([EVENT.apiRequestBody, EVENT.apiResponseBody])`.
- `export const MAIN_AGENT = 'main'`.
- `agentNameFromQuerySource(value)` — `'agent:builtin:general-purpose'` and
  `'agent:user:reviewer'` yield the last segment; `'sdk'`, `'compact'`, anything not
  starting `agent:`, and non-strings yield `null`.
- `agentHintOf(attrs)` — `{name, source:'agent.name'}` when `agent.name` is present,
  else `{name, source:'query_source'}` from the parse above, else `null`.
- `contentMetaOf(log)` — the body-less description of a content record:
  `{bodyLength, bodyTruncated, model, querySource, requestId}`, reading `body_length`
  (falling back to the length of `body`), `body_truncated`, `model`, `query_source`,
  `request_id`.
- `describeEvent` gains cases for the two body events, so the event tail shows
  "<model> request body (<n> chars[, truncated])" instead of falling through.

## 2. `src/store.mjs` — keep the content, and resolve the lane

**Per-session state** added in `newSession`:
- `content: []` — references to the ingested `api_request_body`/`api_response_body`
  log records, in arrival order (they are already in `this.logs`; this is an index, not a
  second copy).
- `subagentToolSpans: Map(toolSpanId -> subagentType)` — filled when a `SPAN.tool` span
  carries `subagent_type` (or `tool_name` `Agent`/`Task`).
- `agentInstances: Map(executionSpanId -> {key, name, firstMs, lastMs})` — filled when a
  `SPAN.toolExecution` span's `parentSpanId` is in `subagentToolSpans`. The two spans
  can arrive in either order, so keep a pending map for the execution-span-first case, the
  same shape as the existing `#applyResultTokenFallback` join.
- `agentIds: Map(agent_id -> executionSpanId)` — filled when a span carrying `agent_id`
  resolves to an instance, so later records of the same subagent resolve in one lookup.

**`#agentKeyOf(session, record)`**, evaluated at query time and not at ingest (span and
log pipelines flush independently, so ingest order proves nothing):
1. `record.spanId` is an instance key → that key.
2. `record.attrs.agent_id` is known → its instance key.
3. walk `parentSpanId` upward through the trace's spans (cap the walk at 16 hops) → the
   first ancestor that is an instance key. This is what attributes `tool_decision` and
   nested tool spans (finding 7).
4. `agentHintOf(record.attrs)` → key `agent:<name>`, a per-type lane. This is the only
   path when traces are off, and it is why bodies stay attributable without spans.
5. otherwise `MAIN_AGENT`.

**Lane list** — `listAgents(session)`, folded into `getSession` as `agents`: one entry
per resolved key with `{key, name, source, firstMs, lastMs, contentCount, requestCount,
toolCallCount}`. `name` is the `subagent_type` for span-resolved instances, the parsed
query-source name otherwise, and `null` for `main`. `source` is one of
`'span'|'agent.name'|'query_source'|'main'`, so a later increment can show how confident
the attribution is. Lifetimes come from the execution span where there is one, else from
the min/max time of that lane's records; `subagent_completed` extends `lastMs`.

**Queries**:
- `queryContent({sessionId, agent = null, sinceMs = 0, untilMs = Infinity, limit = 2000})`
  → the content records in time order, each as
  `{seq, timeMs, eventName, agent: {key, name, source}, spanId, traceId, ...contentMetaOf}`
  — **metadata only, never the body text**.
- `getContextAt({sessionId, agent = MAIN_AGENT, atMs})` → the newest
  `api_request_body` of that lane at or before `atMs`, as the same shape *plus* `body`
  (the exact string as it arrived) — or `null` when that lane has nothing at or before
  that time.

**Memory bound.** Bodies make the count-based log window unbounded in bytes (50 000 logs ×
up to 1 MB). Add a store option `maxContentBytes` (default 256 MB) and a running
`contentBytes` total; when `#evict` finds the total over budget it drops the `body`
attribute of the oldest content records, keeping `body_length`/`body_truncated` so
timings and sizes still draw, and marks them `bodyEvicted: true`. The record itself stays
in the log window and is evicted by the existing age/count rules. Rejected: dropping whole
records (surgery on `this.logs` and its indices for no gain), and a smaller `maxLogs`
default (it would shorten the event tail for everyone). This bound is about memory, **not**
about missing flags — criterion 5 forbids a fallback for recordings made without the
content flags, and nothing here provides one. `#dropSession` must clear the new per-session
maps and subtract their bytes.

## 3. `src/server.mjs` — serve it

- `GET /api/sessions/:id/content` — `agent`, `since`, `until`, `limit` (default 2000,
  max 20000) → `{items:[…]}` from `queryContent`. Metadata only; this is what a timeline
  draws from, so it must stay small.
- `GET /api/sessions/:id/context?at=<ms>&agent=<key>` → `{sessionId, agent, atMs,
  context: <record with body> | null}`. `agent` defaults to `main`, `at` defaults to
  the session's `lastSeenMs`. Unknown session → 404. A lane with nothing at or before
  `at` → 200 with `context: null`; an empty answer is not an error.
- `GET /api/sessions/:id` gains `agents` (the lane list), beside the existing
  `traces`. Rejected: a separate `/api/sessions/:id/agents` route — the session view
  fetches one document already.
- `GET /api/events`: every item gains `agent: {key, name, source}`; the query gains
  `agent`, `sinceMs` and `untilMs` filters (passed through to `queryEvents`); and the
  `body` attribute of content events is **replaced** in the served item by
  `contentMetaOf` fields, so the tail never ships megabytes. `queryEvents`'s `search`
  haystack likewise excludes `body` — stringifying every body on every search would scan
  hundreds of megabytes.
- `/api/stream` needs no change: it already sends `describeEvent` summaries, never attrs.

## 4. `src/persist.mjs`

Raise `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` from 64 MB to 512 MB. With bodies on, `logs.jsonl` passes 64 MB
within a few hundred API requests, and rotation keeps only one previous generation — the
start of a measured session would be gone before the run ends, which is exactly the part a
scrub wants. Nothing else in the file changes. Rejected: keeping more generations (the
loader would have to order N files and the cap stops being a cap).

## 5. `bin/argus.mjs`

Help text only: the `env` line says the block also turns on content — prompts, assistant
responses, tool parameters, tool content and raw API bodies — and that the content lands in
the collector and, with `--persist`, on disk. No new flag, no new format; `renderEnv`
already renders whatever `otelEnvFor` returns in all four formats, which is what makes
criterion 1 hold for every format at once.

## 6. `scripts/demo-emit.mjs`

Per LLM call, emit `claude_code.api_request_body` and `claude_code.api_response_body`
with a small synthetic Messages-API JSON body, `body_length`, `model` and
`query_source`. Per session, emit one subagent: an `Agent` `claude_code.tool` span with
`subagent_type`, its `claude_code.tool.execution` child, two nested `llm_request` spans
carrying `agent_id`, and log events whose `spanId` is the execution span and whose
`query_source` is `agent:builtin:<type>`, closed by a `claude_code.subagent_completed`
event. Without this the demo generator produces exactly one lane and no context at all, so
the increments after this one would have nothing to look at without a live agent.

## 7. Documentation

- `tools/argus/README.md`: the "Sensitive data" section currently states `argus env`
  **deliberately does not** set the content flags — after this change that sentence is
  false and has to say the opposite, naming the four flags plus the content-length
  variable, and stating plainly that prompts, tool arguments and whole API bodies then live
  in the collector's memory and, with `--persist`, in the measurement directory. The
  "Wiring up an agent" example block gains the new lines. The API route table (around line
  539) gains `/api/sessions/:id/content` and `/api/sessions/:id/context`, and the
  `/api/sessions/:id` row mentions `agents`. The "Limits" section notes that a
  measurement with bodies is orders of magnitude larger on disk.
- `skills/argus/SKILL.md`: its route table (around line 77) gains the same two rows.
- `tools/argus-ui/README.md` is **not** touched: the page's views do not change in this
  increment.

## Out of this increment

No file under `tools/argus-ui/` changes. No timeline, no lanes drawn, no scrubbing, no
message-list rendering — those are later increments, and this one only has to put the data
where they can reach it.

Entry points changed: `otelEnvFor`, `EVENT`, `describeEvent`; new exports `CONTENT_EVENTS`, `MAIN_AGENT`, `agentNameFromQuerySource`, `agentHintOf`, `contentMetaOf`.

return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. Everything below is `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, in
`tools/argus/test/`, whose conventions live in `tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md` — that doc
exists, is current, and nothing I read contradicts it; it also says the doc grows a line
whenever the suite does, so its per-file list gets updated for the cases below.

Record fixtures are hand-built literals in the shape the decoder produces, exactly like the
existing `log`/`span` builders in `store.test.mjs`. The attribute shapes below are taken
from real captured telemetry (Claude Code 2.1.226), so use them verbatim rather than
inventing plausible ones:
- main-session body event: `eventName 'claude_code.api_request_body'`, attrs
  `{model, body:'{"messages":[…]}', body_length:'113845', body_truncated:'true',
  query_source:'sdk'}`, `spanId` = the interaction span id.
- subagent body event: same event name, attrs `{model, body, body_length,
  query_source:'agent:builtin:general-purpose'}` (**no `agent.name`** — that is the
  verified gap), `spanId` = the `claude_code.tool.execution` span id of its `Agent` call.
- dispatching spans: `claude_code.tool` with `{tool_name:'Agent',
  subagent_type:'general-purpose', tool_use_id}`, and its child
  `claude_code.tool.execution` with `parentSpanId` = that tool span.
- a subagent tool call: `claude_code.tool` `{tool_name:'Bash', agent_id:'a132…'}` whose
  `parentSpanId` is the execution span, and a `claude_code.tool_decision` log whose
  `spanId` is a `tool.blocked_on_user` span under that Bash span (two hops up).

## Cases

**Criterion: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in every format.**

1. `tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs` — unit. `otelEnvFor('http://localhost:4318')`
   carries `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS='1'`, `OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES='1'`,
   `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS='1'`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT='1'`,
   `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES='1'`, and a `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH` whose
   number is ≥ 100000 (assert the bound, not the exact figure: the point is "large enough
   that a whole context is not truncated", and the figure is tuning).
   Run: `node --test tools/argus/test/claude.test.mjs`.
2. Same file — unit. `otelEnvFor(endpoint, {traces:false})` still carries the four
   content flags but **not** `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT`, which needs spans to land anywhere.
3. `tools/argus/test/config.test.mjs` — process level, `execFile` of `bin/argus.mjs`
   as the existing `settings`-format case does. One case covering all four formats:
   `env`, `env --format json`, `env --format dotenv`, `env --format settings` each
   carry `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES` with value `1` — parsed out of the JSON for the two
   JSON formats, matched as `export OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES="1"` for shell and
   `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1` for dotenv. This is the case that pins "every format it
   prints"; the other flags are covered at unit level by case 1.
   Run: `node --test tools/argus/test/config.test.mjs`.

**Criterion: the collector stores what those events carry and serves it per agent, per time.**

4. `tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs` — unit. Two body events and one response body
   ingested for one session; `queryContent({sessionId})` returns them oldest-first with
   `timeMs`, `eventName`, `bodyLength`, `bodyTruncated`, `model` — and **no `body`
   field on any item**. Run: `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`.
5. Same file — unit. `getContextAt` returns the newest request body at or before the
   asked time: three bodies at t, t+1000, t+2000; asking at t+1500 returns the second, with
   its `body` string intact; asking at t-1 returns `null`.
6. Same file — unit, attribution through the span tree. Ingest the dispatching `Agent`
   tool span, its execution span, a main-session body event and a subagent body event as
   described above. `getSession(id).agents` holds exactly two lanes: `main`, and one
   named `general-purpose` keyed by the execution span id. `queryContent({agent:<that
   key>})` returns only the subagent's record.
7. Same file — unit, ordering independence. The same fixtures ingested with the execution
   span **before** its parent `Agent` tool span produce the identical two lanes; span and
   log pipelines flush separately, so neither order may be assumed.
8. Same file — unit, the parent walk. A `tool_decision` log two hops below the execution
   span resolves to the subagent lane, not to `main`.
9. Same file — unit, no traces at all. A body event carrying only
   `query_source:'agent:builtin:reviewer'` (no spans ingested) lands in a lane named
   `reviewer` with `source` naming the query source, distinct from `main`; a body event
   with `query_source:'sdk'` lands in `main`.
10. Same file — unit, lane timing. `getSession(id).agents` gives each lane a `firstMs`
    and `lastMs` that cover that lane's own records and no other lane's.
11. Same file — unit, the content byte budget. `new TelemetryStore({maxContentBytes: <a
    few hundred bytes>})`; after three bodies the oldest is served with `body: null` and
    `bodyEvicted: true` while its `bodyLength` still reports the original size, and the
    newest still has its body. This pins that the bound drops content and never the
    timeline metadata.
12. Same file — unit, no leak. After a session is dropped by the existing eviction, its
    content index and agent maps are gone and `queryContent` for it is empty. Follow the
    eviction case already in the file for how a drop is provoked.
13. `tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs` — integration over a real server on port 0.
    `GET /api/sessions/:id/content` answers 200 with the content records including

    `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`.
14. Same file — integration. `GET /api/sessions/:id/context?at=<ms>` answers 200 with the
    full `body` of the nearest request body at or before that time; `?at=` before every
    body answers 200 with `context: null`; an unknown session answers 404.
15. Same file — integration. `GET /api/events` no longer ships body text: after a body
    event is ingested through the OTLP route, its item carries `bodyLength` and no `body`
    attribute, and carries a resolved `agent`.
16. Same file — integration. `GET /api/events?agent=<key>` returns only that lane's
    events, and `GET /api/sessions/:id` carries the `agents` lane list.

## Left untested, deliberately

- **Recordings made without the content flags.** Criterion 5 puts them out of contract: no
  case may assert a fallback, a degraded rendering or a compatibility notice for a session
  whose telemetry carries no bodies. Do not add one. (Case 9 is not that case: it covers a
  session that *has* bodies but no traces.)
- **The exact value of `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH` and the new 512 MB persist
  rotation default.** Both are tuning constants; a test pinning either would fail on a
  better number. Case 1 asserts only the lower bound that makes contexts parseable.
- **`scripts/demo-emit.mjs`.** No suite covers the demo generator today and this increment
  does not start one; it is a development aid, exercised by running it.
- **The live-CLI verification itself.** It needs an authenticated `claude` run and the
  network. It was performed once by hand for this plan and its results are recorded as
  findings; it is not automatable in the suite.
- **`bin/argus.mjs` help wording.** The suite doc's rule is that messages are asserted as
  absences, never as wordings.

## What is already red

I did not run any command in the check list, not even once as a baseline: reading the code
tells me the suite is green on this branch (nothing is half-built here — `git log` shows
only the increment-branch bookkeeping commit), and a full run buys no fact I could not
state from that. The first run belongs to whoever runs it downstream. The one thing I did
run was outside the suite entirely: a real measured `claude -p` session against a local
collector on port 4319, to settle the two verification criteria (which flag emits bodies,
and what agent attribution actually arrives). That collector was stopped and its output
written under the scratchpad, not the repository.

Verified against a real measured Claude Code 2.1.226 run: bodies are emittable, but they carry no agent.name — attribution comes from query_source and from the tool.execution span id of the dispatching Agent call, and that gap is recorded rather than papered over.

increments.title: The timeline is the session view, with a lane per agent
increments.goal: Opening a session lands on a timeline that draws one lane for the main session and one per subagent, each spanning that agent's lifetime, with the existing technical views kept reachable underneath it.
criteria: Opening a session in the argus UI lands on the timeline view.
The previous technical views (event tail, traces, raw inspectors) stay reachable from the timeline and are subordinate to it, not the other way round.
The timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent, each agent lane spanning that agent's lifetime, so any vertical slice answers which agents are running at that moment.
Where the telemetry attributes subagent traffic incompletely, the lanes show what is attributable and the gap is reported as a finding.

increments.title: Each lane shows its activity and its context growth
increments.goal: Fill the lanes: activity over time, and behind it the context size over time, so where token consumption grows is visible on the timeline itself.
criteria: Each lane shows that agent's activity over time — tool calls and API requests — positioned at the times they happened.
Behind that activity each lane draws the context size over time as a curve or area.
Growth in token consumption is readable from the timeline alone, without opening any detail.

increments.title: Scrubbing the session, and following it live
increments.goal: Give the timeline its time control: a point in time the human moves backward and forward over the whole recorded session, and a live mode that follows the newest data.
criteria: The timeline can be scrubbed backward and forward to any point of the recorded session.
A live mode follows the newest data as it arrives.
Scrubbing away from the head leaves live mode, and a control returns to it.

increments.title: Selecting a lane shows that agent's context and tools at that moment
increments.goal: Answer the two per-agent questions at the chosen time: what the context looked like, and which tools that agent had used with what parameters.
criteria: Selecting a lane at the chosen time shows that agent's (or the main session's) context as of that moment: the body of the nearest API request at or before that time.
That context is rendered as a structured message list — system prompt, user, assistant, tool call, tool result — with each block collapsed to one line carrying its size.
Each block expands to the exact full text.

Selecting a lane at the chosen time also shows the tools that agent has used up to that moment, with tool name and the call's parameters, so "which tools, and what for" is answerable per agent and per time.
